title.narrative: Girls in Tech: Transforming Futures of Palestinian girls and invest in closing the digital divide between adolescent boys and girls and ensure girls are provided equal opportunities to excel in STEM fields.

description.narrative:
Palestinian women alongside with men have made significant contributions across various sectors including their role in socio- economic development and family and community life. However, women and girls continue to face entrenched discrimination and rights violations.
In Education, Palestinian women have made meaningful progresses. Literacy rates for women have improved significantly, and women exceeded the number of men in Palestinian universities. As for the percentage of female students enrolled in Palestinian higher education institutions, it reached 62% out of the total number of students enrolled in higher education institutions in 2021-2022, of whom about 10% are enrolled in the ICT major, (59% among males, and 41% among females), and about 3% are enrolled in natural sciences, mathematics and statistics (28% among males, and 72% among females). However, there remains a gap in translating education into workforce participation. The unemployment rate among women participating in the labor force was about 40% compared to 20% among men in 2022. Those who do work often face wage gaps and limited opportunities in leadership positions. Women are more likely to work in education, healthcare, and informal sectors.
This intervention will focus on building the capacity of adolescent girls in West Bank in applying digital technologies for the resilience and development of their communities, while nurturing their well-being and promoting their personal and professional development. In particular, the activity is developed to support school students, mainly girls, in creating digital solutions to address women's and girls' equal rights and empowerment using coding, robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) through project-based learning and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) education approaches.
Project Goal This initiative aims to inspire and support adolescents (80% girls, 20% boys) to embark on a learning journey to be capable of contributing to re-building and re-shaping their communities, their personnel development and their futures. Through the project, students will develop their 21st century, digital technology and innovation skills that can help them gain and create employment while fostering more resilient and sustainable communities by addressing such issues and challenges related to human rights, livelihood, health issues and climate change. All activities will be directed to promote women's and girls' equal rights and empowerment and support the active participation and engagement of girls in all project activities.
Project objectives • Enhance female students’ creativity, sense of collaboration and team building and strengthen their problem-solving, presentation, technical and digital skills, ensuring their personal and professional development. • Increase investments in closing the digital divide between adolescent boys and girls and ensure girls are provided equal opportunities to excel in STEM fields. • Develop and implement innovative, technology-driven solutions that promote women's and girls' equal rights and empowerment by leveraging emerging technologies to enhance access to opportunities and foster economic and social development opportunities for all.
(GEM) 3 project This initiative in ICT and STEM aims to reduce disparities and promote women's and girls' equal rights and empowerment by addressing structural barriers, biases, and skill gaps in sciences and ITC. It recognizes that empowering girls in technology, support societies and economies development. Additionally, the proposed capacity building activities help bridge the skills gap by encouraging girls to pursue careers in innovation and STEM fields.
